claims.claim: The rumqttc 0.24.0 crate root docs list mqttbytes v4 as the default (re-exporting mqttbytes::v4::* plus mqttbytes::*), with v5 available as a separate mqttbytes::v5 module — the top-level MqttOptions/AsyncClient/Event API is the v3.1.1 (v4) surface.
claims.stance_target: rumqttc 0.24.0's primary/default API is MQTT v3.1.1 (v4); MQTT 5 lives in a separate v5 module
claims.quoted_support: pub use mqttbytes::v4::*; pub use mqttbytes::*; Modules§ mqttbytes mqttbytesv5

claims.claim: rumqttc 0.24.0's documented reconnection model is 'Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop' — automatic reconnection, not automatic re-subscription.
claims.stance_target: rumqttc 0.24.0 automatically reconnects the transport but does NOT automatically re-subscribe; subscriptions must be re-established by the application after reconnect
claims.quoted_support: Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop ... Since the eventloop is externally polled (with iter()/poll() in a loop) out side the library and Eventloop is accessible, users can ... Access internal state for use cases like graceful shutdown or to modify options before reconnection

claims.claim: rumqttc 0.24.0 documentation explicitly warns that looping on connection.iter()/eventloop.poll() is required to run the event loop, and blocking inside the loop blocks connection progress — the poll() loop is the sole driver of the connection.
claims.stance_target: Any ha-linux-agent MQTT task design must keep polling the eventloop; a stalled poll loop stalls the whole connection
claims.quoted_support: Looping on connection.iter()/eventloop.poll() is necessary to run the event loop and make progress. ... Blocking inside the connection.iter()/eventloop.poll() loop will block connection progress.

claims.claim: rumqttc 0.24.0's Event enum (yielded by eventloop.poll()) has exactly two variants — Incoming(Incoming) and Outgoing(Outgoing) — with no Reconnect variant, and the type alias Incoming covers packets including ConnAck.
claims.stance_target: In 0.24.0 a reconnect can only be inferred by seeing a second Event::Incoming(Packet::ConnAck); no Event::Reconnect exists until PR #1052 merges
claims.quoted_support: pub enum Event { Incoming(Incoming), Outgoing(Outgoing), } — Events which can be yielded by the event loop

claims.claim: AsyncClient::disconnect() exists in rumqttc 0.24.0 as 'pub async fn disconnect(&self) -> Result<(), ClientError> — Sends a MQTT disconnect to the EventLoop', alongside try_disconnect(); the full method surface also includes subscribe, subscribe_many, unsubscribe, publish, publish_bytes, ack, and from_senders.
claims.stance_target: The repo's pinned rumqttc 0.24.0 exposes AsyncClient::disconnect() for graceful shutdown; no API gap blocks it
claims.quoted_support: pub async fn disconnect(&self) -> Result<(), ClientError> — Sends a MQTT disconnect to the EventLoop

claims.claim: The 0.25.1 AsyncClient surface is method-for-method identical to 0.24.0's (new, from_senders, publish, try_publish, ack, try_ack, publish_bytes, subscribe, try_subscribe, subscribe_many, try_subscribe_many, unsubscribe, try_unsubscribe, disconnect, try_disconnect) — 0.25.1 adds no auto-resubscribe, v5-session, or reconnect-signal method to AsyncClient.
claims.stance_target: Upgrading from rumqttc 0.24.0 to 0.25.1 does not change the AsyncClient API surface relevant to connection lifecycle; auto re-subscription is absent in both
claims.quoted_support: impl AsyncClient — pub fn new ... from_senders ... publish ... try_publish ... ack ... try_ack ... publish_bytes ... subscribe ... try_subscribe ... subscribe_many ... try_subscribe_many ... unsubscribe ... try_unsubscribe ... pub async fn disconnect(&self) -> Result<(), ClientError> — Sends a MQTT disconnect to the EventLoop ... try_disconnect
